author: Lowe, 1841

note.en: A big-eyed shark with a tail as long as its body, living in deep open water by day and rising to the surface at night. A GBIF record at Río Sixaola is a fossil tooth; no living local record. Costa Rica and ICCAT protect it.
note.es: Un tiburón de ojos grandes con una cola tan larga como su cuerpo, que vive en aguas abiertas profundas de día y sube a la superficie de noche. Un registro de GBIF en el río Sixaola es un diente fósil; no hay registro vivo local. Costa Rica e ICCAT lo protegen.

evidence: A GBIF record at Río Sixaola (Alto Guayacán dataset) is a fossil tooth
No local record found; FishBase lists it for Costa Rica and the Western Central Atlantic (coast not stated)

sources.t: IUCN Red List: Alopias superciliosus, Vulnerable

recWhy: No record on Costa Rica's Caribbean coast in the file (general range or Costa Rica only).

marks.en: Extremely long upper tail lobe and very large eyes that reach onto the top of the head.
marks.es: Lobulo superior de la cola extremadamente largo y ojos muy grandes que llegan a la parte superior de la cabeza.
